title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part IX of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (sequel to La Longue Marche). Fix a group scheme G over S, e.g. G = GL(2) over Ẑ. Fix two sections ρ, σ, for example ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 3 in PGL2) and σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (order 2 in PGL2). The previous page defines SM_{ρ,σ} = S𝒢*_{ρ,σ} ×_S SG, where S𝒢*_{ρ,σ} is the scheme of solutions of the 'loop equation' in G. It also defines, via abelianization π̂_{0,3}^{ab} ≅ Ẑ², a homomorphism Ĝ_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}/(±1). This page takes the 'positive' part Ĝ⁺_{0,3}, which lands in SL(2,Ẑ)/(±1).

The programme: build a group M̃_{0,3} with a canonical map to the product (1). Then put a group law on SM_{ρ,σ} so that this map is a homomorphism. In effect this is a G-valued, scheme-theoretic 'linearization' of the GT-type group.

Step 1, the 'special' variant SM̃_{0,3}.
- π̂_{0,3} is the free profinite group on two generators, with three inertia generators ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞.
- T̂_{0,3} is the profinite (outer) Teichmüller-type group.
- M̃_{0,3} is a group of automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} containing the inner ones, with M̃_{0,3}/π̂_{0,3} ⊂ T̂_{0,3}. Each u permutes the conjugacy classes of the ℓ_i, sending ℓ_i to a conjugate of ℓ_{u(i)}^λ, where λ ∈ Ẑ* is the multiplier.
- SM̃_{0,3} consists of the tuples (u, g_0, g_1, g_∞), with g_i ∈ π̂_{0,3} chosen conjugators: u(ℓ_i) = int(g_{u(i)}^{-1})(ℓ_{u(i)}^λ).
- The product is (u',g')(u,g) = (u'u, g'_i·u'(g_i)), stated 'or something analogous (left/right!)' and restricted to λ = λ' = 1.

Next page: the kernel of SM̃ → M̃ is {(1,f_i) : f_i ∈ L_i}, where L_i ≅ Ẑ is the centralizer of ℓ_i. This gives 1 → Ẑ³ → SM̃_{0,3} → M̃_{0,3} → 1.

Next page continued: using that u commutes with the order-3 rotation ρ up to an inner element g = [u,ρ], one f_i determines the other two by f_{i+1}^{-1} = g·ρ(f_i^{-1}). Consistency requires the cocycle condition g·ρ(g)·ρ²(g) = 1, which is the analogue of the hexagon relation of GT.

In modern terms: SM̃ is the group of automorphisms equipped with tangential-base-point (conjugator) data at the three punctures. Drinfeld's normalization σ(x) = x^λ, σ(y) = f^{-1} y^λ f is the gauge-fixed slice g_0 = 1, g_1 = f of this Ẑ³-torsor family.
errors: Formula (5) as written, g''_i = g'_i·u'(g_i), is only correct when u' fixes the indices 0, 1, ∞. With convention (4), where g is indexed by the target puncture, composition gives g''_j = g'_j·u'(g_{u'^{-1}(j)}), and the multipliers multiply (λ'' = λλ'). Grothendieck himself flags the doubt ('ou un truc analogue (à gauche/à droite!)') and retreats to λ = λ' = 1. A reindexing is still needed if u permutes the punctures.

Kernel description (next page): one needs that the centralizer in π̂_{0,3} of each inertia generator is the procyclic group it generates. This is true for free profinite groups but is used without comment.

ideas.what: Group of automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} together with chosen conjugators (g_0, g_1, g_∞) for the three inertia generators, with a twisted product law, forming an extension by Ẑ³ of the automorphism group
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms with tangential-base-point data; unnormalized version of Drinfeld's (λ,f) description of GT̂, or Ihara-type special automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps for tangential base points
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (Teichmüller tower, choices of base points); this explicit construction is not, to my knowledge, published

ideas.what: Abelianization homomorphism Ĝ_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/(±1), with the positive part landing in SL(2,Ẑ)/(±1)
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT̂ / Aut(F̂_2) on H_1, i.e. the abelianization map Aut(F̂_2) → GL_2(Ẑ)

ideas.what: Programme to put a group structure on SM_{ρ,σ} = S𝒢*_{ρ,σ} × SG (solutions of the loop equation in an arbitrary group scheme G, plus a section of SL2) so that M̃_{0,3} → SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) is a homomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Scheme-theoretic / linear-algebraic analogue of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group attached to (G,ρ,σ); loosely comparable to representation-valued or pro-algebraic versions of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (closest: Drinfeld's pro-unipotent GT, Enriquez's elliptic variants)

ideas.what: Recovering the conjugators f_{i+1} from f_i via the defect g = [u,ρ] of commutation with the order-3 rotation, with cocycle condition g·ρ(g)·ρ²(g) = 1
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon (order-3) relation of GT expressed as a 1-cocycle for Z/3

missed.claim: Grothendieck aims to endow SM_{ρ,σ}, built from solutions of the loop equation in a general group scheme G, with a group law making the map from the GT-type group M̃_{0,3} multiplicative. This is a 'linearized' GT-like group scheme defined for any (G,ρ,σ). The thread is announced here and continued around pp. 390 and 559ff; the construction for general G does not appear in the literature as such.
missed.quote: on va construire une variété de groupe M̃_{0,3} (cf p. 390), qui s'envoie canoniquement dans le produit (1), ce qui nous amènera à définir une structure de groupe sur SM_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give algebraic-group (e.g. GL2- or SL2-valued) quotients or shadows of GT̂ via the loop equation, related to but distinct from the pro-unipotent/Lie-algebra approaches (Drinfeld, Ihara) and elliptic GT. It could provide computable invariants of GT̂ elements.

deep.surprise_reason: The concrete construction on this page (automorphisms plus conjugators, a Ẑ³ extension, the order-3 cocycle) is essentially the familiar Drinfeld/Ihara description of GT̂ in unnormalized form, with a sloppy product formula. Only the announced programme of a group law on loop-equation schemes SM_{ρ,σ} for a general G is somewhat unusual. It is merely sketched here.
transcription_corrections: First line: the group is probably Ĝ⁺_{0,3} (consistent with the previous page's Ĝ_{0,3}), not 𝒱̂⁺_{0,3}.
'de façon : munir ledit morphisme multiplicatif' is likely 'de façon à rendre ledit morphisme multiplicatif'.
In (3), g_0, g_1, g_∞ ∈ π̂_{0,3} (lowercase π, the fundamental group), not Π̂_{0,3}.
'où λ est la multiplication de u' should read 'le multiplicateur de u'. The next clause is likely 'et i ↦ u(i) l'action de u sur l'ensemble {0,1,∞} des classes de lacets'.
'(à gauche / à gauche!)' is probably '(à droite / à gauche!)'.
The quotient written Π̃_{0,3} = M̃_{0,3}/π̂_{0,3} is likely a script M or T with a tilde; uncertain.
